title: Record ETH Leverage on Binance: Contrarian Bet or Liquidation Setup?
subTitle:
ETH open interest on Binance has hit an all-time high while price sits near multi-year lows. The derivatives data points in two directions simultaneously, and which one plays out depends on whether spot demand follows.

Key Takeaways
Binance ETH perp volume hit 5.57M units vs 290K spot - Perp-Spot Imbalance at 0.90, near ATH.
30-day Z-score of 2.53 confirms the derivatives-spot divergence is historically abnormal.
Binance ETH open interest reached a new all-time high of 3.7M ETH, holding 44% market share.
Weekly Taker Buy/Sell Ratio moved from 0.95 to 1.16, buy-side flow has caught up with sellers.
On Binance, ETH perpetual futures volume has reached approximately 5.57 million units while spot market volume sits at just 290,000 units. The ratio between the two has pushed the Perp-Spot Imbalance indicator to 0.90, near its all-time high. The 30-day Z-score of 2.53 confirms this divergence is not a temporary fluctuation. A Z-score above 2.0 means the current reading sits more than two standard deviations above the recent historical mean, and statistically, this is significantly outside normal market behavior.

In plain terms: the overwhelming majority of ETH trading activity on Binance is currently happening through leveraged derivatives contracts, not through people actually buying or selling the underlying asset. That distinction matters because derivatives volume does not represent genuine supply and demand. It represents leveraged bets on price direction, and those bets need to be settled one way or another.
What Perp-Spot Imbalance and Z-Score Actually Mean
The Perp-Spot Imbalance is a ratio comparing perpetual futures trading volume to spot trading volume on the same exchange. When the ratio is low, most activity happens in the actual asset, with organic buyers and sellers determining price. When the ratio climbs toward 1.0, derivatives activity is almost entirely dominating price discovery.
A Z-score measures how far a current reading deviates from its historical average, expressed in standard deviations. A Z-score of 2.53 means the current imbalance sits 2.53 standard deviations above its 30-day mean, a reading that in a normal distribution would occur less than 1% of the time. In market terms, this confirms the derivatives-spot divergence is historically abnormal, not just elevated.
The risk this creates is mechanical. When derivatives dominate spot activity by this margin, the market becomes extremely sensitive to position unwinds. A relatively small price move can trigger a cascade of liquidations, automated stop-losses and margin calls that then accelerate the move further in either direction. The actual supply and demand picture gets buried under layers of leveraged positioning, making price action harder to read as a signal of genuine conviction.
Open Interest at an All-Time High, Into Weakness
According to CryptoQuant's ETH open interest data, Binance has recorded a new all-time high with nearly 3.7 million ETH now positioned in futures contracts on the platform. Binance's share of total Ethereum open interest has simultaneously crossed 44%, cementing its dominance in the ETH derivatives market.

Open interest measures the total number of outstanding futures contracts that have not been settled. A rising open interest figure means new money is entering the derivatives market, with traders opening positions rather than closing them. At 3.7 million ETH, this represents a historically significant level of leveraged exposure concentrated on a single exchange.
The context makes the data notable. Open interest typically climbs alongside price, as traders add leverage into strength to amplify momentum. The current setup inverts that pattern. Leverage is being added into weakness, with ETH trading near multi-year lows around $1,650.
The supply context behind that price level is covered in detail in a separate Coindoo analysis, which documents how exchange reserves have fallen from 21 million to 14.5 million ETH over the same period despite the price decline.
That inversion has two possible explanations: traders collectively believe the bottom is in and are positioning for a recovery, or they are adding leverage at a structurally fragile price level where a failure to hold could trigger a violent unwind.
Taker Buy/Sell Ratio: The One Bullish Signal in the Data
The positioning data contains one directional shift worth isolating. According to CryptoQuant's Taker Buy/Sell Ratio, the weekly average on Binance moved from 0.95 to 1.16, meaning buy-side flow has pulled even with selling pressure after months of seller dominance.

The Taker Buy/Sell Ratio measures the ratio of aggressive buy orders to aggressive sell orders in the derivatives market. A ratio below 1.0 means sellers are more aggressive than buyers, initiating trades at the bid.
A ratio of exactly 1.0 means the two sides are in equilibrium, while a ratio above 1.0 means buyers are more aggressive than sellers. The move from 0.95 to 1.16 indicates that buy-side flow has not just recovered, but is now meaningfully outpacing selling pressure. With traders actively hitting the ask to open long positions rather than waiting on the sidelines, the data suggests the market is treating these multi-year price lows as an accumulation opportunity rather than a warning sign.
This is the one data point in the set that tilts directionally positive. It does not override the structural risk flagged by the Perp-Spot Imbalance, but it does suggest the leverage being added at these levels is predominantly long-biased rather than short-biased.
What the Data Cannot Resolve
These two readings, record open interest at multi-year price lows and a taker ratio shifting toward buy-side equilibrium, describe the same market from different angles and reach different conclusions.
The open interest and imbalance data signal structural fragility. A market running at a 0.90 Perp-Spot Imbalance with a 2.53 Z-score has historically preceded sharp, fast moves when leverage gets unwound. The mechanism is not directional. Liquidation cascades can run in either direction depending on which side of the trade gets squeezed first.
The taker ratio data signals nascent accumulation. Traders moving from net-sell to net-neutral in derivatives flow, while open interest reaches an all-time high, could reflect genuine contrarian positioning by participants who believe current prices represent value.
Which interpretation proves correct depends on one variable the on-chain data cannot supply: whether spot demand follows the derivatives positioning. If genuine buyers enter the spot market and absorb sell pressure, the long-biased open interest could act as fuel for a sharp recovery. If spot demand fails to materialize and price breaks lower, the same open interest becomes the accelerant for a liquidation cascade. The data identifies the setup. It does not resolve the outcome.

Bitcoin jumped on news from Iran—but instead of just focusing on the bounce, we should pay attention to two small details. 

I don’t quite agree with the simple narrative that this sudden surge in Bitcoin can be categorized as "geopolitical easing leading funds back to risk assets." 

After Trump called off the strike plans against Iran, Bitcoin did indeed bounce for a bit, with WTI crude oil falling simultaneously. The surface logic seems sound: a ceasefire expectation equals a rise in risk appetite, benefiting long-duration assets. But the problem is that this equation pins all the gains on a single piece of news that could reverse at any moment—this isn’t a trend signal that can withstand scrutiny. 

My first reaction was to dig into two not-so-obvious clues, which carry more information than Bitcoin itself. 

The first clue is that the U.S. has seized $1 billion in crypto assets as leverage in the negotiations with Iran. This isn’t just a side note—it signifies that cryptocurrencies have moved from the "retail battlefield" into the toolbox of sovereign negotiations. Regardless of how you feel about this signal, it will influence how the U.S. defines the overall regulatory framework for crypto assets moving forward. This is not something that can be digested in a single day’s news. 

The second clue is Trump’s nomination of the former SEC chairman to become the national intelligence director. This is someone who has "waded through" the crypto regulatory cycle being brought into the intelligence sphere. This news won’t pump the market tomorrow, but it points to a longer-term structural change: the U.S. is funneling individuals with practical crypto policy experience into decision-making roles. The next time a crypto-related bill comes up for discussion, you’ll find that the people drafting the legislation aren’t amateurs. 

VELVET is currently trending at number one, having just crossed the top 100 market cap threshold, so attention is certainly coming in. However, during times of intense geopolitical news, the traffic in the trending lists tends to get scattered repeatedly, and whether this temporary interest can turn into sustained holding will depend on whether it can stabilize after the volatility ends. 

My judgment is that over the next two days, the short-term direction won’t depend on what Trump said today, but on whether there are any advancing bills or executive actions this week. The questions raised by senators at the nomination hearings, and the specific positioning of crypto assets within the Iran negotiation framework—these two undercurrents can tell you more about the market tone than the oil price gap and Bitcoin’s sudden bounce. 

Right now, I’ll be watching three directions: whether there are signs of easing liquidity in USD, whether the public statements from senators reflect bipartisan attitudes towards the nomination, and whether trending coins like VELVET can recover depth after the volatility ends. In short-term trading, the biggest fear isn’t misjudging the direction, but mistaking noise for trend confirmation.

比特币借伊朗消息跳了一下——但比反弹更该看的，是两件小事

我不太同意把这次 比特币 的瞬时拉升简单归类为"地缘缓和所以资金回风险资产"

特朗普叫停对伊朗的打击计划之后，比特币确实跟着弹了一段，WTI 原油同步回落。表面逻辑走得通：停火预期等于风险偏好回升，久期资产受益。但问题在于，这一套等式把所有涨幅都挂在了同一条随时可能反转的消息上——这不是经得起检验的趋势信号

我第一反应是去翻两条不太起眼的线索，它们的信息量比 本身大得多

第一条，美国在伊朗谈判中扣押了 10 亿美元加密资产作为谈判筹码。这件事不是小插曲——它意味着加密货币已经从"散户战场"进入了主权级谈判的工具箱。无论你对这个信号持什么态度，它都会影响美国后续如何定调加密资产的整体监管框架。这不是一条日内新闻就能消化完的

第二条，特朗普提名前 美国证监会 主席 出任国家情报总监。一个在加密监管周期里"趟过水"的人，被送进了情报口。这件事明天不会拉盘，但它指向一个更长期的结构性变化：美国正在把有过加密政策实战经验的人往决策层输送。下次再有加密相关法案进入议程，你会发现写条文的人已经不是外行了

VELVET 这一轮上热搜第一，市值刚过百名门槛，注意力确实进来了。但在地缘消息密集的窗口里，搜索热榜的流量天然会被反复打散，能不能从短暂关注变成沉淀持币，要看异动结束后深度能不能稳住

我的判断是：接下来两天短线方向不取决于特朗普今天又说了什么，而取决于这周有没有推进中的法案或行政动作落地。提名听证会上议员的提问方向，以及加密资产在伊朗谈判框架里的具体定位——这两条暗线，比油价跳空和 比特币 瞬时反弹更能告诉你后市基调

我现在会先看三个方向：美元流动性有没有配合松动的迹象，议员对 提名的公开表态能不能反映出两党态度，以及 VELVET 这类热搜币在异动结束后能不能修复连续深度。短线交易最怕的不是方向判断错，而是把噪音当成趋势确认

The core logic is: assets shouldn't just have to choose between 'locking them up for yield' and 'taking them out to use', but should continue participating in underlying yield production while maintaining liquidity. 
Assets like uniBTC and brBTC are significant because they transform the traditionally clunky BTC positions into liquidity tokens that are more suitable for on-chain finance. What users hold at the core is BTC value, while what they use on-chain is a more flexible asset form. This way, BTC isn't just a position waiting for price swings; it can also engage in lending, liquidity, yield strategies, and more scenarios to maximize capital utilization. 
The bigger highlight of Bedrock 2.0 is its ability to expand in the multi-asset direction. If BTCFi only sticks to 'deposit coins for yield', the ceiling isn't very high; but if it can connect staking assets, liquidity tokens, yield distribution, and ecological incentives, it resembles a foundational infrastructure for asset efficiency. It's not about who can shout the highest APY, but who can create a stable closed loop of underlying assets, yield sources, and on-chain usability. 
The value of $BR  should also be viewed within this closed loop. It's connecting not just trading sentiment but also user participation, ecological incentives, governance expectations, and long-term capital accumulation in Bedrock 2.0. For me, what makes Bedrock worth paying attention to is its attempt to push BTC from being a 'store of value' to 'productive capital'. Recently withdrew from a liquidity pool, and while the page profits looked decent, I found out there was quite a bit of slippage when I actually tried to exit. At that moment, I was reminded of an old issue: with on-chain projects, it's not just about how smooth the entry is, but also about how clean the exit can be. 
I'm looking at @Bedrock 's Bedrock 2.0 from this perspective. Many BTCFi products love to say 'BTC can make you money', but what really determines whether users are willing to hold assets long-term is often not the highest yield, but the exit path, liquidity depth, and the stability of asset conversion. $BTC  is a hard asset, and once it enters the on-chain yield system, what users care most about becomes: can I smoothly exchange the receipt back for the underlying asset? Will there be significant discounts during market fluctuations? Will large exits crash the pool? 
One of the key technical focuses of Bedrock 2.0 is to address the liquidity issues of BTC entering DeFi in advance. uniBTC isn't just a symbol for displaying balances; it needs to handle asset mapping, circulation, conversion, and scenario integration. A mature BTC yield system can't just provide a smooth experience when users deposit; it must also maintain sufficient stability during redemption, transfer, trading, and cross-scenario usage. 
Here, it's all about underlying risk control capabilities. For example, the liquidity configuration of the asset pool, compatibility between different BTC assets, redemption window arrangements, and price deviation control during extreme market conditions—these are the keys to whether Bedrock 2.0 can go the distance. Yield can attract people in, but the exit mechanism determines whether they dare to stay. 
The long-term value of $BR  will also depend on whether it can bind this underlying infrastructure capability. If Bedrock can make the entry, circulation, usage, and exit of BTC smoother, then BR will be carrying not just short-term hype, but the entire protocol value of the BTCFi asset layer. 
My current method for evaluating projects is a bit clumsy: don't just look at how they get you in, first check how they get you out. The real aspects to observe in Bedrock 2.0 lie here. #bedrock  #BTC #ETH

我看 @Bedrock  的 Bedrock 2.0，也是从这个角度看。很多 BTCFi 产品喜欢讲“BTC能赚钱”，但真正决定用户敢不敢长期放资产的，往往不是最高收益，而是退出路径、流动性深度和资产兑换稳定性。$BTC  本身是硬资产，一旦进入链上收益系统，用户最关心的就变成：我拿到的凭证能不能顺利换回底层资产？市场波动时会不会出现明显折价？大额退出会不会把池子砸穿？
Bedrock 2.0 的技术重点之一，就在于把 BTC 进入 DeFi 后的流动性问题前置处理。uniBTC 不是单纯拿来展示余额的符号，它需要承担资产映射、流通、兑换和场景接入的功能。一个成熟的 BTC 收益系统，不能只在用户存入时体验顺滑，也要在赎回、转移、交易、跨场景使用时保持足够稳定。
这里拼的是底层风控能力。比如资产池的流动性配置、不同 BTC 资产之间的适配、赎回窗口的安排、极端行情下的价格偏离控制，这些才是 Bedrock 2.0 能不能走远的关键。收益可以吸引人进来，但退出机制决定人敢不敢留下。
$BR 的长期价值，也要看它能不能绑定这种底层基础设施能力。如果 Bedrock 能把 BTC 的进入、流通、使用和退出都做得更顺，BR承接的就不只是短线热度，而是整个 BTCFi 资产层的协议价值。
我现在看项目有个笨办法：别只看它怎么让你进去，先看它怎么让你出来。Bedrock 2.0 真正值得观察的地方，也在这里。#bedrock  #BTC #ETH

Changing Doesn't Always Mean Advancing
For a long time, I assumed that any change was a sign of progress.
The logic seemed reasonable.
If something is constantly evolving, then it should be advancing.
However, over time, I started to notice an interesting difference.
Many things change.
But not all of them improve.
Some simply transform.
Others evolve in a way that allows them to remain relevant when the environment starts to shift.
And that difference might be more important than it seems.
Because perhaps one of the most widespread beliefs is that change and progress are the same thing.
But maybe that’s not always the case.
Perhaps a significant part of progress depends on the ability to change while preserving what made a system valuable from the start.
It was precisely reflecting on some conversations around @Ethereum_official  #Ethereum $ETH  that I revisited this idea.
Because when we observe systems that have persisted for years, we rarely find stagnation.
But we also don’t find random changes.
We find something different.
A constant adaptation that tries to respond to new challenges without completely losing its identity.
And that raises an interesting question.
Does progress simply appear because something changes?
Or does it emerge when a system learns to evolve while remaining recognizable?
After all, changing can be relatively straightforward.
The hard part seems to be evolving without losing what made the change worthwhile.

Cambiar No Siempre Significa Avanzar
Durante mucho tiempo asumí que cualquier cambio era una señal de progreso.
La lógica parecía razonable.
Si algo evoluciona constantemente, entonces debería estar avanzando.
Sin embargo, con el tiempo empecé a notar una diferencia interesante.
Muchas cosas cambian.
Pero no todas mejoran.
Algunas simplemente se transforman.
Otras evolucionan de una forma que les permite seguir siendo relevantes cuando el entorno comienza a modificarse.
Y esa diferencia puede ser más importante de lo que parece.
Porque quizá una de las creencias más extendidas sea que el cambio y el progreso son la misma cosa.
Pero tal vez no siempre ocurra así.
Tal vez una parte importante del progreso dependa de la capacidad de cambiar conservando aquello que hizo valioso a un sistema desde el principio.
Fue precisamente reflexionando sobre algunas conversaciones alrededor de @Ethereum_official  #Ethereum $ETH que volví a pensar en esta idea.
Porque cuando observamos sistemas que han permanecido durante años, rara vez encontramos inmovilidad.
Pero tampoco encontramos cambios aleatorios.
Encontramos algo diferente.
Una adaptación constante que intenta responder a nuevos desafíos sin perder completamente su identidad.
Y eso plantea una pregunta interesante.
¿El progreso aparece simplemente porque algo cambia?
¿O aparece cuando un sistema aprende a evolucionar sin dejar de ser reconocible?
Después de todo, cambiar puede ser relativamente sencillo.
Lo difícil parece ser evolucionar sin perder aquello que hizo que el cambio valiera la pena.

A lot of newbies see ETH drop from 4800 to 1668 and their first reaction is, "It's going lower, I'll buy at 1000." I thought the same way at first.

Now the trading volume is increasing, which indicates that someone is stealthily building their position. If it breaks past 1720, we could see a nice pump.

content:
【ETH在筑底吗？】

很多新手看到ETH从4800跌到1668，第一反应是"还要跌，等1000再买"。我当初也是这么想的。

但你们知道吗？上周ETH悄悄涨了2.3%，而整个市场还在恐慌。恐惧指数只有12，几乎是历史最低。按理说应该继续暴跌对吧？结果它反而稳住了。

Now my account sits at over twenty million, and it doesn’t even phase me anymore. 💰
What I've built over these years is worth more than cash—it's discipline and mindset.
🔹Positioning: Never go full throttle, only move 20% at a time.
If I’m down 10%, I cut losses, no holding. A few bad trades? No biggie, one trend will bring it all back.
🔹Bottom fishing: Not doing it. Trying to catch the bottom in a downtrend is like catching a knife with bare hands.
Once a trend is established, wait for a pullback to jump in, the win rate is way higher.
🔹Meme coins: Not touching them. Multiplying a few times in a few days? The whales pump it up just to hand it to you.
🔹Indicators: Only watch MACD. Buy when there's a golden cross below the zero line and it’s above the zero line; sell when there's a death cross above the zero line, reduce position first.
🔹Adding to positions: Don’t add when you're down, only add when you’re making gains. Follow the volume surge and price breakout.
Six words to sum it up: Go with the flow, control your losses, don’t rush.
If the line is trending up, hold; if it turns, bail out.
There’s no holy grail, it’s all about self-control.

# Someone borrowed 18,000 ETH from Aave and transferred it all to Binance—Is this a pump and dump?

On-chain data just caught: a wallet borrowed 18,000 ETH from Aave in the last two days, worth about $45 million to $55 million at market price. Then, it was all transferred to Binance.

This move is something seasoned traders know well—DeFi lending → transfer to CEX → high probability of selling. Either cashing out and running, or going short. Holding borrowed coins for the holidays? 

Last time I saw this kind of play was in March 2024 on Solana, where someone borrowed $15 million worth of SOL from Marginfi and transferred it to Coinbase. Everyone in the group was shouting, "The whale is about to dump!" I was skeptical, thinking, "Transferring to an exchange doesn’t necessarily mean selling, what if they’re participating in an IDO?" Three days later, SOL dropped by 12%. I still held over 200 SOL at the time, watching my profits shrink by nearly $30,000.

So seeing 18,000 ETH heading to Binance this time, my first reaction isn’t analysis but a chill down my spine.

ETH is already on a downward spiral. From $4,000, it plummeted to $1,900, more than a halving. It’s been hovering around $2,000 for almost two weeks. If this 18,000 ETH really gets dumped, the $2,000 support level is unlikely to hold.

Of course, it could also be a smoke screen. Transferring to an exchange doesn’t 100% equal selling. But on-chain data doesn’t lie: borrowing → transferring to an exchange, the probability of shorting/selling is far greater than anything else. This risk isn’t worth the gamble.

I’ve placed some buy orders around $1,700-$1,800, small positions in batches. If it really drops to that level and I miss out, no big loss; if I do get in, I won’t panic.

What do you think this whale is really up to?

# SpaceX is ringing the bell on NASDAQ today, and the crypto market just got drained

SpaceX is going public today, with a whopping $75 billion— the largest IPO in human history. Retail investors got a slice of $22.5 billion, with 30% allocated to them, unprecedented.

Where's the cash coming from?

The crypto market.

Last night, BTC shot up to 63179, looking like it was about to rebound. But once the SpaceX blood-letting effect kicked in, it plummeted straight down to 62642. In just 24 hours, 120,000 traders got liquidated, with $332 million going up in smoke. Longs got wrecked for $193 million, shorts for $139 million— a double whammy, no one escaped.

I fell into the same trap back when Coinbase went public in 2021. A week before the IPO, the crypto market was buzzing like it was on steroids, everyone shouting "compliance is bullish, institutions are coming in!" I actually bought into it, adding to my COIN position near 380. But on the IPO day, it started to tank, dropping 15% in a week. I held for three months and finally cut it at 280. Since then, I've learned my lesson— big IPOs mean blood-letting, not bullish signals.

This time, SpaceX is much bigger than Coinbase. GSR's OTC trading director put it bluntly: "Cryptocurrency has become a financing tool; investors need to find the cash for the $75 billion IPO, and it has to come from somewhere."

What stings even more is that the AI space is queuing up—Anthropic and OpenAI are also going public. The CEO of INDIGO said it straight: "AI is clearly more attractive than cryptocurrency." It’s not pleasant to hear, but it’s the hard truth. The crypto market is no longer the only high-risk, high-reward game in town.

In the short term, the SpaceX effect will continue to drain for a few days. Don't rush to catch the falling knife. But if BTC can hold in the 60000-62000 range for a week or two, after the SpaceX hype cools down, short covering and sidelined funds might come back in, leading to a swift and strong rebound.

SpaceX今天正式上市，750亿美元——人类历史上最大的IPO。光散户配额就分了225亿，30%给散户，前所未有。

📰 Crypto Market Hotspot Dispatch

1. Bitcoin Core Private Broadcast Exposes Privacy Risks
The Bitcoin Core team has flagged that the new -privatebroadcast feature introduced in version 31.0 has a privacy vulnerability, where under specific network conditions, the trading sender's IP might be identifiable by receiving nodes, compromising user anonymity and broadcast security. The official fix has been confirmed and will roll out in version 31.1. Users relying on node-level privacy should tread carefully with this feature in the short term, as the market once again turns its attention to the balance between Bitcoin's infrastructure performance, privacy, and usability.

2. Coinbase Urges Blockchain to Accelerate Quantum Migration
Coinbase's Quantum Advisory Board has released a new report urging blockchain developers to kickstart quantum migration preparations ASAP. They believe address reuse, public key exposure, and long-dormant assets could become systemic risks in the future. The report estimates that about 7 million Bitcoins could theoretically be more vulnerable to future quantum attacks. While the quantum threat is still hypothetical, the industry is already planning migration, freeze limits, and gradual transitions, making quantum security a hot topic.

3. Fidelity Stablecoin FIDD Integrates with Uniswap Liquidity
Uniswap has disclosed that asset management giant Fidelity has chosen it as the liquidity layer for its stablecoin FIDD, and the related liquidity pool is now live. This indicates that traditional financial institutions are becoming more aggressive in embracing DeFi infrastructure for stablecoin issuance and on-chain liquidity deployment. If subsequent trading depth, redemption efficiency, and institutional access go smoothly, FIDD could become an important bridge connecting traditional asset management products with on-chain markets, bringing new attention to the Ethereum ecosystem and DEX applications.

4. US Discusses Crypto Regulatory Clarity and Enforcement Tools
Reports indicate that White House officials, lawmakers, and law enforcement recently held meetings focusing on the Blockchain Regulatory Certainty Act and crypto crime enforcement tools. Signals show that the US is simultaneously pushing for clearer industry rules and enhanced enforcement capabilities, attempting to provide clearer boundaries for developers and infrastructure participants, while also improving efficiency in combating illicit fund flows and on-chain crime. Regulatory and compliance expectations will continue to sway market sentiment.

5. Ripple and Bitso Expand Cooperation to Advance Latin American Stablecoin Settlements
Ripple and Bitso are expanding their partnership, planning to bring Bitso's Mexican peso stablecoin MXNB onto the XRP ledger to support the settlement needs of Latin American enterprises. This move illustrates that stablecoin competition is extending from dollar-pegged assets to local fiat scenarios, with cross-border payments, enterprise settlements, and regional financial infrastructure becoming key focus areas. If MXNB generates real transaction flow on the enterprise side, it could further enhance the usability of the XRP ledger in the Latin American payment ecosystem.
